kept.spine: At present nothing presses Rundgate. Its defenses read strong, past the point where pressing them would cost more than it would gain.
The country around is an active frontier, and the walls and the garrison hold a perimeter that keeps most trouble from ever pressing it.
faces: A traveller says nobody at the gate asked what he had passed on the road, though he had come ready to tell it.
A serjeant on the wall says the gate is barred at dusk without fail, and nobody argues the hour with him.
A priest of one of the parishes holds that the men who watch the country are prayed for in the same breath as the roads.
One of the aldermen says no complaint about the nights beyond the wall has reached the hall at all.
The watch hold that what complaints there are stop at the gate and go no further.
An innkeeper says the talk at his tables runs to who stands the nights, and never to what waits past them.
A soldier of the garrison says the drills draw no crowd from the town, not even the curious.
A guild factor reckons the trades foot the toll that pays for the watch at the gate, and counts the keeping of it as everyone's due, not the trades' alone.
A stallholder says the stalls go up the same whether the country is quiet or not.
A bailiff says a dispute over the toll is heard the day it is brought, and the country beyond the gate has never brought one.
The elders say the young stand the nights and the old say how they are stood.

kept.poolKey: Invasion & War: walls AND professional garrison
kept.spine: A traveller is stopped and counted at the gate before he is let through. What lies past it is a place that keeps its own paid soldiers, walls and all.
faces: The men who hold the ways in say a stranger pays his toll at the gate, and the gate settles its own account with the hall in its own time.
A woman who keeps the hall books holds that a stranger who pays at the gate has paid the town in full, whatever is said to him at the gate itself.
A clerk of the court says anyone who paid a toll may dispute it before the bench, a stranger the same as a carter.
A pedlar says his pack was opened at the gate and nothing taken from it beyond the toll owed.
A man who drinks where the carters drink holds that the town was never asked whether it wanted soldiers, only what keeping them costs.

kept.spine: The court here sits, and keeps no cell for anyone it judges. What its law can take from a person is coin, or a place in the town.
faces: A night patrolman says whatever is caught after dark is settled after dark, there being no cell to hold a man until morning.
The officers of the court say they hear by daylight what the watch already settled in the dark, and ask it nothing first.
A clerk in the hall reckons the purse has never run to a cell, and does not say who first asked for one.
At the market a stallholder says a short weight goes before a magistrate and comes back as a sum. The scales it was weighed on stay on his stall.
A priest of one of the parishes holds that the parish keeps a place for a man once he is dead, and the town keeps none for him while he lives.
A journeyman says a fine comes out of a man's earnings and is forgotten, though the mark it leaves on his work is not.
The drinkers of the district say a man with a house here pays and stays. A man without one is sent off, and the table loses him.
A drover says there is nothing to take from a man who owns nothing in the town. The town is left with the one thing it can still do with him.
A gatekeeper reports being handed a man and a direction, and given no reason for either.
A serjeant of the garrison says what comes at the town is the garrison's business, and the people turned out of it are not.

kept.spine: A working balance holds here at Rundgate. The law is present and so is crime, and neither one has the run of the town.

kept.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
kept.spine: What is known of Rundgate so far comes from a first look, honest about what has been seen and silent about what has not.
A stranger at Rundgate is not robbed outright, but is quietly told how matters are arranged here, since the danger runs organized rather than sudden.
Entry points here are the town's own to control, and keeping them is what buys Rundgate its choice of where trouble is met.
A standing force keeps Rundgate's defense as its trade, paid and answerable for the work like any other.
The town pays for some of its soldiers outright, and keeps track of exactly which ones, treating them accordingly.
A traveller reaching Rundgate finds a hall whose business is the sort of trouble a garrison is not suited for, and finds that hall busy.
Passing through Rundgate's gate, a stranger is measured in some way he cannot quite name, and nobody offers to explain it to him.
The city walls and gates at Rundgate are kept in better order than the watch meant to stand behind them, the pay for standing there being the part of the work that keeps coming up short.

kept.poolKey: Logistics & Supply: Granary with road supply
kept.spine: Stores are kept at Rundgate and the town is fed in by the roads. The roads are the risk in that, and the granary is what buys time against it.
